validity.recommendation: P3176 is a real, substantially/fully built 880km trunk gas pipeline running from Gryazovets, Gryazovetsky District, Vologda Oblast, to KS Slavyanskaya, Kingisepp District, Leningrad Oblast (the Nord Stream 2 head compressor station). It is officially item 9 of Приложение N4 to Russian government decree No. 816-r ('Развитие газотранспортных мощностей ЕСГ Северо-Западного региона, участок Грязовец - КС Славянская', sudact.ru consolidated text read), and is the subject of at least 10 independent primary/trade-press documents describing its construction (2018-2022), contractors (Stroygazmontazh as GC; Gazregion, Lengazspetsstroy, Krasnodargazstroy, Neftegazkomplektmontazh, SPKh Nauka as subcontractors), investor/owner (Gazprom PJSC via Gazprom Invest LLC), and operating subsidiaries (Gazprom Transgaz Ukhta for the Vologda Oblast segment, Gazprom Transgaz Saint Petersburg for the Leningrad Oblast segment/terminus). NOT a duplicate: distinct from the parallel Gryazovets-Vyborg corridor (P0746/P5585, a separate, older, 917km/1400mm pipeline built earlier to feed the original Nord Stream), from Gryazovets-Leningrad (P5534/P5535), and from the Ukhta-Torzhok variants (P1439 etc.) -- this is the newer corridor built specifically circa 2017-2022 to feed Nord Stream 2's head station while also serving NW/Central Russia gasification and the Ust-Luga industrial zone (confirmed by the RIA/Neftegaz/decree capacity-increase reporting explicitly naming both purposes). Fuel=Gas and PipelineType=transmission are directly and repeatedly confirmed ('МГП' = магистральный газопровод in nearly every source). CAVEAT (not a disqualifying concern, but material -- see status_reviews[] for the full discussion): the newest dated primary evidence of construction/commissioning activity found in this research pass is Dec-2022 (compressor-shop commissioning); no source dated 2023-2026 was found that explicitly confirms the trunk is presently transporting gas. GEM's own wiki text itself hedges 'As of July 2023 ... presumed to be operating' rather than stating it as confirmed fact. This is flagged as a caveat on the Status verdict, not an existence/classification/duplicate problem with the row itself.

status_reviews.staleness_rule: No LastUpdated value visible in the worklist for this row. Newest dated primary evidence found in this pass is 29-Dec-2022 (ukhta-tr.gazprom.ru press release, 6 compressor shops commissioned) and Mar-2022 (komiinform.ru, line strings under working pressure) -- both roughly 3.7 years old at the time of this review (Sep-2026). Under the 2y-shelved/4y-cancelled dormancy rule this gap alone would start to raise a staleness flag, EXCEPT that rule is written for pipelines whose only evidence is construction/proposal-stage activity going quiet; here the evidence shows construction essentially complete and commissioning underway/complete by end-2022, i.e. the project had already crossed into (or was on the direct threshold of) operating status. A stalled PRE-completion project going quiet for years is a shelved/cancelled signal; a project that had already reached commissioning and then simply stopped generating fresh press coverage is the unremarkable, expected pattern for a completed pipeline (completed infrastructure does not keep making news). No dormancy/delay/cancellation signal was found anywhere in this research -- the absence of post-2022 sourcing reads as 'nothing newsworthy happened' rather than 'something went wrong.'

status_reviews.researcher_notes: VERDICT RATIONALE: I am recommending 'confirm' (operating stays operating) rather than 'unclear', but flagging real uncertainty the reviewer should weigh. What IS solidly established: construction essentially complete by late 2021 (186km finished, plus the parallel Stroygazmontazh 300+km award from 2018), and compressor-station/line commissioning activity ongoing through at least Dec-2022, with no negative signal (no delay, suspension, or cancellation report found anywhere). What is NOT established by any source I could read: an explicit post-2022 statement that the trunk is presently in commercial operation and transporting gas. GEM's own wiki text hedges this exact point ('As of July 2023, construction works have been complete, with commissioning works underway. The pipeline is presumed to be operating' -- read for leads only, not cited). I attempted to find a 2023-2026 dated confirmation: TASS's 2024 Ust-Luga-complex article (tass.ru/ekonomika/21104811) was inaccessible after escalation (WebFetch 403, curl returned only a 1784-byte bot-block stub; no Wayback capture attempted before this research pass ended) and would in any case have been about the downstream gas-chemical complex's OWN construction progress (46% complete end-2024 per WebSearch), not this pipeline's status directly. Weighing it: (1) the pipeline's domestic Leningrad Oblast gasification purpose (explicit in the RIA/Neftegaz/decree capacity sources: 3.4 bcm/y earmarked for 'потребители Ленинградской области') is a live, ongoing need independent of Nord Stream 2's mothballed status or the Ust-Luga complex's unfinished construction -- an operating designation is defensible on that domestic purpose alone, consistent with this batch's export-leg-dormancy rule (flow to a mothballed export leg =/= non-operating, if the pipe itself serves domestic purposes and is physically intact); (2) a fully-built, commissioned Gazprom trunk near a major compressor station sitting idle for 3+ years with zero news coverage of that idleness would itself be a newsworthy oddity in Russian energy press, and none was found; (3) but I could not produce a single dated 2023+ primary source stating 'in operation.' On balance I recommend 'confirm' over 'unclear' because nothing found argues against operating and multiple lines of evidence argue for substantial completion + an ongoing domestic rationale, but I want this reasoning fully visible rather than a clean unqualified confirm.
